title: Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

reports.title: Second member of the Milwaukee Police Department charged with misuse of license plate reader system
Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

summary:
Milwaukee Police Detective Tehrangi Chapman was charged with felony misconduct in public office and misuse of a GPS device. A complaint says he admitted using the Flock license plate reader system 20 times to track two people, violating department policy. It says he searched one person's plate 17 times from January 2024 to January 2025 and installed a GPS device on that vehicle. He also searched another person's plate three times in January 2025, listing training as the reason. Chapman, a 22-year veteran, has been suspended since March 13 and is due in court July 17.

The charges follow Officer Josue Ayala, who pleaded guilty to attempted misconduct in June and resigned after being accused of misusing the system. Milwaukee officials called the new charges troubling, and the department announced changes to system access and audits after Ayala was charged. Some Wisconsin communities, including Verona, Dane County, UW-Madison, and Kaukauna, have ended or declined to renew Flock contracts. Flock Safety said misuse is unacceptable and its audit trails help detect abuse.
